title: Would a fake policy date work?
hook: Place a pretend policy before the real one. What should its contrast show?

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: rerun diff-in-diff with placebo dates; real designs show no fake effects.

misconception: Treating fake treatment dates as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: rerun diff-in-diff with placebo dates; real designs show no fake effects.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Before a true policy, control outcomes are 10,11,12 and treated are 12,13,14. Put a placebo date between the first two points. What fake DiD appears in this pre-policy window?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-fake-treatment-dates/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Control series[10,11,12,13,14], treated[12,13,14,20,21]. True post starts index3; fixed trend difference2 pre,7post. Fake date index1 sees no shift before true policy; teach placebo falsification cannot prove absence of confounding.
